title: Blackstone Chicken Cutlets with Warm Buttermilk Ranch Gravy
description: Thin chicken cutlets steam in a skillet on the griddle while dill, chives and cultured buttermilk give the gravy its ranch flavor.
equipment: 10-inch cast iron skillet with fitted lid

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breast
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

steps.title: Even the cutlets
steps.text: Butterfly {chicken} into cutlets. Between two sheets of parchment, gently tap the thick ends with the flat face of a meat mallet to an even 3/8 inch.

steps.title: Heat the broth on the griddle
steps.text: Set the cast iron skillet on the Blackstone over one medium burner. Add {broth}, {onion} and {garlic} and cover for 5–8 minutes until the broth simmers.

steps.title: Poach the cutlets
steps.text: Nestle the cutlets into the broth, cover and lower the burner to medium-low. Maintain a bare simmer for 4–8 minutes, turning once and removing each cutlet at 165°F. Hold covered with a little broth.

steps.title: Boil the broth
steps.text: Transfer the poaching broth to the HexClad and boil on the stovetop for 1 minute.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Temper the buttermilk
steps.text: Whisk a little hot gravy into {buttermilk} in a bowl. Take the skillet off heat and gradually whisk the warmed buttermilk mixture back into the gravy.

steps.title: Add the ranch herbs
steps.text: Stir {chives} and {dill} into the finished gravy. Keep warm over residual heat to retain the fresh herb flavor.

steps.title: Sauce and serve
steps.text: Slice the cutlets across the grain and turn them in the warm gravy. Divide between bowls and spoon the remaining gravy over both.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/4 cups for two. Make ahead: Mince the herbs the same day. Refrigerate them wrapped until the buttermilk goes in. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours, or within 1 hour outdoors above 90°F. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Cultured buttermilk gravy can turn grainy after freezing. For freezer meal prep, freeze chicken in the starch-thickened base for up to 2 months and add the buttermilk and herbs after reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm the cutlets in their gravy, stirring gently to keep it smooth covered in the HexClad over medium-low with a splash of water. Stir or turn occasionally and check from 6 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses tangy buttermilk. For gentler Option B, use skim milk and keep the herbs. Unsweetened plain oat milk works for a dairy-free gravy. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 211 kcal, 34.5 g protein, 6.6 g total carbohydrate, 4.1 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 170 mg sodium. Includes all the chicken and sauce in the listed recipe. Sodium varies with the broth.
